messages.subject: Multinomial and Dirichlet prior
parts:
Dear forum,

I would like to use INLA for infering sum-to-1 proportions (modalities of a categorical variable), hence without any covariate. I use multinomINLA, for example:

dat <- data.frame(y=factor(c(rep("A",10),rep("B",60),rep("C",30),rep("D",0))),x=1)
X <- multinomINLA(formula=y~x, data=dat)
X$summary.multinomial

seems to be pretty good (necessary to for force x=1?). Now my question is: how I can transform my prior knowledge on these proportions (usually in a Dirichlet prior) in the "hyper" argument. In the example above I was assuming (because expecting 10% of level "D", not present in the sample) a Dirichlet(6.44, 32.20, 19.32, 5.85).

Thanks in advance, erik.
PS: I wish everyone a more peaceful year 2021.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Multinomial and Dirichlet prior
parts:
Hi,

I'm not familiar with multinomINLA, but I guess it use the poisson eqv,
see the (rather long) vignette about this issue for theory and examples.

There is currently no good way to transfer a dirichlet prior for the
proportions to an eqv prior for the latent field. It should be possible
with using offsets and controling variances (like N(m_i, var_i), and
chose those to get what you want, approx).

Best
H
